'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[2021 Damascus bus bombing]]
***Two [[improvised explosive device|bombs]] attached to a [[Syrian Army|military]] bus detonate as it passes under Jisr al-Rais bridge in [[Damascus]], killing 14 people. Minutes later, military [[shellfire]] kills at least 10 civilians in [[Ariha]], [[Idlib Governorate]]. [https://bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-58930309 (BBC News)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**Sixteen civilians are killed after armed militants raided villages in [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Beni]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/21/sixteen-civilians-killed-in-overnight-eastern-drc-village-attacks (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Nepal floods]]
**The death toll due to floods and [[landslide]]s in western [[Nepal]] increases to 77. The [[government of Nepal|government]] has pledged aid to the hardest-hit areas. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/nepal-floods-and-landslides-kill-at-least-77-2582286 (NDTV)]
*[[Mount Aso]] in [[Kumamoto Prefecture]], [[Japan]], erupts, sending smoke 3,500 meters into the sky. The [[volcanic eruption|eruption]] began around noon local time. Chief Cabinet Secretary [[Hirokazu Matsuno]] says that there are no reports of injuries but that they are currently investigating reports of climbers on the mountain before the eruption. [https://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/14464596 (''The Asahi Shimbun'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya]]
****[[Kenya]]n [[President of Kenya|President]] [[Uhuru Kenyatta]] lifts the nationwide [[curfew]] that had been in place since March 2020 and allows [[place of worship|places of worship]] to be filled to two-thirds of their capacity as the number of [[COVID-19]] cases decreases. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-10-20/kenyan-president-lifts-night-time-curfew-as-virus-cases-decline (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Senegal]]
****[[Senegal]] reports zero COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours for the first time since the beginning of the [[pandemic]]. [https://www.news24.com/amp/news24/africa/news/covid-19-senegal-logs-zero-new-cases-for-first-time-since-pandemic-began-20211020 (News 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]]n [[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] approves the [[Mikhail Mishustin's First Cabinet|cabinet]] proposal for non-working days for employees from October 31 until November 7 amid a persistent increase in the number of COVID-19 cases and deaths. [https://www.voanews.com/a/putin-imposes-week-long-workplace-shutdown-to-combat-covid-19-/6278358.html (VOA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia]]
****The [[Serbia]]n [[Government of Serbia|government]] announces that they will introduce COVID-19 [[Vaccine passports during the COVID-19 pandemic|health passes]] for all indoor cafés and restaurants, which will be mandatory beginning from October 23 at 10:00 p.m. [https://rs.n1info.com/english/news/serbia-introduces-covid-19-passes-for-indoor-cafes-and-restaurants/ (N1)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****The [[Government of the United Kingdom|British government]] signs an agreement to secure 480,000 courses of [[Molnupiravir]] produced by [[Merck Sharp and Dohme]], and 250,000 courses of Ritonavir produced by [[Pfizer]], where both of them need to be approved by health regulator. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-uk-strikes-deals-for-two-antiviral-drugs-to-help-combat-coronavirus-surge-this-winter-12439406 (Sky News)] 
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
***[[Singapore]] reports a record 18 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 264. [https://www.todayonline.com/singapore/covid-19-3862-new-cases-spore-record-18-deaths-reported-day-brings-tally-264 (''Today'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
***The [[Food and Drug Administration]] authorizes [[booster dose]]s of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna]] and [[Janssen COVID-19 vaccine]]s, as well as allow Americans to choose a different vaccine from their original inoculation as a booster. [https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2021/10/20/1047093449/the-fda-authorizes-moderna-and-j-j-covid-vaccine-boosters (NPR)] 

'''International relations'''
*[[President of Russia]] [[Vladimir Putin]] says that he will not physically attend the [[2021 United Nations Climate Change Conference|COP26 climate summit]] in [[Glasgow]]. Expert state that Russia's potential absence coult threaten efforts to get leaders to negotiate a new deal to stall rising global temperatures. However, the Kremlin states that Putin could still appear virtually. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-58977993 (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Stoneman Douglas High School shooting]]
**Nikolas Jacob Cruz, who is accused of the 2018 [[mass shooting]] at [[Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School]] in [[Parkland, Florida]], [[United States]], [[plea]]ds guilty on all 34 [[criminal charge|charges]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/10/20/us/nikolas-cruz-parkland-shooting-guilty/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*An indirect [[2021_Barbadian_presidential_election|presidential election]] was held to choose the first ever [[President of Barbados]].  The outgoing [[Governor-General of Barbados]], Dame [[Sandra Mason]], was the only candidate nominated; Mason will be sworn in on 30 November, the 55th anniversary of Barbadian independence from the [[United Kingdom]]. The government of Barbados announced in September 2020 that they would transition to a republic by that date. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-58993728 (BBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''

**Researchers at [[NYU Langone Health]] in [[New York City]] announce that a team of surgeons last month, led by Dr. [[Robert Montgomery (physician)|Robert Montgomery]], successfully [[Xenotransplantation|attached]] a genetically-modified [[pig]] [[kidney]] to a [[Brain death|brain dead]] patient for two days without [[Transplant rejection|rejection]].
